catalog.title: Capture labeled activations
catalog.mac: Research methods: Author request, review inputs, then open execution and evidence. Both CLIs use science interview/draft/publish and the same managed engine.
outputs: Immutable run with pinned inputs, provenance, and inspectable probe evidence.
catalog.restriction: Bounded binary probe workflow. Predictive accuracy is not causal evidence or calibrated probability. Capture uses the Python engine; fitting and evaluation use shared CPU owners. Legacy readers are preserved.

actions.authorityReason: Inspect staged scientific inputs and execution resources without execution or authorship.
Execute a reviewed scientific operation and retain its scientific output type.

access.restriction: Calls the existing route with its existing service role and scientific gates. Request path parameters, query and body remain explicit; this adapter does not change execution topology or retry mutations.

interview.title: Capture labeled activations
interview.purpose: Read one declared residual site for labeled text, saving reusable fitting, selection, and final-test files. This runs the model without changing its weights.

fields.label: Prepared model
fields.help: Choose the model on the execution host. No weights are downloaded by capture.

fields.label: Labeled text
fields.help: UTF-8 JSONL: id, group, text, label (true/false), and split (fit, selection, or finalTest). Keep related examples in the same group. Copy the probe data instructions for examples and review prompts.

fields.label: Layer to observe
fields.help: Zero-based decoder block. A fixed layer avoids selecting a layer using final-test results.

fields.label: Before or after the block
fields.help: residualPre reads the block input; residualPost reads its output. This is not an individual weight.

fields.label: Text rendering
fields.help: raw uses native special tokens. chatTemplate uses one user message and a generation cue.

fields.label: What the text represents
fields.help: prompt or completeText. Capturing complete text does not establish performance on partial responses. Chat rendering supports prompt only.

fields.label: Positions to read
fields.help: lastNonPadding reads the final token present. eachNonPadding reads every token; the row label then applies to every prefix, which must make sense for your task.

fields.label: How to assign data roles
fields.help: explicit uses each row’s split. groupHash omits split and assigns whole groups by a stable seeded 60/20/20 hash. It does not guarantee balanced small splits.

fields.label: Group split seed
fields.help: Only affects groupHash. Record it before looking at outcomes.

fields.label: Maximum text examples
fields.help: Captures the first N file rows. Start small to check costs, class balance, and tokenization.

fields.label: Maximum tokens per example
fields.help: Long inputs are truncated. The report saves the actual token IDs and observed positions.

fields.label: Maximum activation rows
fields.help: Every observed position consumes a row. Capture stops with a repair if the cap or 64 MiB JSON budget is exceeded; it never silently drops extra rows.

fields.label: Model precision
fields.help: float32, bfloat16, or float16; choose a prepared unquantized model. Actual activation dtype is recorded.

fields.label: Execution device
fields.help: cuda on a GPU runner, mps on a suitable Mac Python engine, or cpu for a small check. No native MLX capture is claimed.

interview.claimBoundary: An activation classifier predicts the supplied labels in this population. It does not establish that the model uses the predicted feature causally.
questions: What do the labels mean, and which related examples belong in one group?
Which data are for fitting, choosing settings, and final assessment?
